frontiers.target: Initial function census over RAW_LOAD_MODULE (starting with _main)
frontiers.matches: RESOLVED: the '_main at file offset 0x639' anchor was wrong by exactly 512 bytes due to an address-space double-conversion bug -- the self-relative CALL fixup's resolved value (load-module offset 0x439) was already a file offset (relative to CS:IP=0000:0000 at file offset 512, per docs/startup-binding-evidence.json), and 512 was mistakenly added to it a second time. Re-derived directly from raw bytes: the CALL instruction is E8 at file offset 764 with disp16=0x013A at file offset 765-766 (not 765-767 as originally logged); target = IP_after(255, seg-relative) + 314 = 569 (seg-relative) = file offset 1081 = 0x439. File offset 1081 is exactly the STARTUP_C0S/RAW_LOAD_MODULE manifest boundary and disassembles to the expected '55 8B EC' (push bp; mov bp,sp) prologue followed by a Turbo C stack-check idiom. Full initial census (tools/function_census.py) then found 193 candidate functions spanning file offset 1081-46179 (~45KB), with zero overlaps and zero truncated functions; no further prologue matches occur anywhere in the remaining ~126KB of RAW_LOAD_MODULE, suggesting the _TEXT code segment ends around file offset ~46179 and the rest is _DATA/_BSS. See docs/function-census.md and docs/function-census.json.
frontiers.first_unresolved_fact: N/A for this milestone -- closed. Follow-on frontiers (segment-boundary confirmation, semantic naming, matching-C promotion of specific functions) are tracked as new entries below.
frontiers.leverage: Unblocks systematic per-function classification and matching-C promotion work across the ~45KB code region; also strongly suggests the code/data segment split point (~file offset 46179), which was previously completely unknown.

frontiers.target: Confirm _TEXT/_DATA segment boundary at approximately file offset 46179
frontiers.matches: docs/function-census.json's 193-function census (built from a '55 8B EC' prologue scan) finds zero candidate function starts anywhere past file offset 46179 in the 172,336-byte RAW_LOAD_MODULE region, which is circumstantial (absence-of-pattern) evidence that Turbo C++'s _TEXT segment ends near there and DGROUP (_DATA+_BSS) follows.
frontiers.first_unresolved_fact: No OMF segment directory survives in the linked/packed executable, so this boundary is inferred only from the absence of prologue-shaped bytes, not proven. It's also possible some code region uses a different calling idiom (frameless leaf functions, hand-written ASM) that the scan cannot see, which could hide code further into the file.
frontiers.unblock: Cross-reference against every CALL/JMP target discovered within the 1081-46179 code region (see 'unmatched_call_targets' in docs/function-census.json) to confirm none point past 46179; separately, look for recognizable ASCII string data or structured table patterns starting near 46179 as positive evidence of _DATA rather than just absence of code patterns.
frontiers.leverage: Would convert an inferred code/data split into a confirmed one, unblocking safe wholesale treatment of the tail ~126KB as data-track work (Phase 2 data/asset census) rather than code.

frontiers.target: Classify and semantically name the 193 census functions; promote first matching-C candidates
frontiers.matches: docs/function-census.json provides id/start/end/size/has_sub_sp/calls/notes for 193 functions. Several strong candidates were spot-checked: F_A460 (9 bytes, IN AX,DX) and F_A469 (11 bytes, IN AL,DX + XOR AH,AH) look exactly like Turbo C++ 1.00 runtime's inport()/inportb(); F_850A (12 bytes) wraps INT 21h AH=9 (DOS print string), consistent with a runtime string-output helper; F_04FC and F_088E contain many repeated 'imul dx' idioms (struct-array indexing) and are promising candidates for the game's own actor/sprite/tile access code.
frontiers.first_unresolved_fact: None of these have been compiled/OMF-bound/byte-compared yet -- they are disassembly-pattern guesses only, not proven matches.
frontiers.unblock: Pick the smallest, cleanest candidates first (F_A460/F_A469 inport/inportb are the best starting points since Turbo C++ 1.00's runtime source for these is well-known/tiny) and run them through the same compile -> OMF-parse -> bind -> exact-byte-compare loop as tools/recover_startup_binding.py, following docs/matching-phase.md's proof standard.
frontiers.leverage: First real matching-C promotions inside RAW_LOAD_MODULE (as opposed to the already-closed STARTUP_C0S library-recognition milestone), establishing the end-to-end proof loop for game code, not just linked-in runtime library code.

end_state: Independent source modules (matching C, matching ASM, structured data/assets) compile, assemble, and link with a historically faithful toolchain such that the resulting unpacked executable image is byte-identical to the original, addresses emerge from module composition rather than being copied, and the image can subsequently be re-packed with LZEXE 0.91 to reproduce the original DAVE.EXE exactly. EGADAVE.DAV resources are simultaneously reconstructed from human-readable canonical sources (images, tables) plus deterministic encoders.
